cues: The same reagent, potassium hydroxide, gives two different products depending on the solvent.
In water, hydroxide acts as a nucleophile, and bromoethane gives ethanol: substitution.
In hot alcohol, hydroxide acts as a base.
It pulls off a hydrogen from the carbon next to the halogen, the beta carbon, and the molecule loses H B r to become ethene: elimination.
text: Now a classic trap. The same reagent, potassium hydroxide, gives two different products depending on the solvent. In water, hydroxide acts as a nucleophile, and bromoethane gives ethanol: substitution. In hot alcohol, hydroxide acts as a base. It pulls off a hydrogen from the carbon next to the halogen, the beta carbon, and the molecule loses H B r to become ethene: elimination.
